name: Nahshon
overview: Nahshon was a male leader from the tribe of Judah, known as the son of Amminadab and brother of Elisheba. He served as the head of the tribe of Judah during the census in the time of the Exodus. His leadership role is specifically noted in the book of Numbers.
namesAndTitles: The name Nahshon means 'small viper' in Hebrew. This proper name, found in Exodus 6:23, does not appear to have been given directly by God but carries a distinct meaning within the biblical text.
familyAndRelationships: Nahshon was the son of Amminadab and the brother of Elisheba, as recorded in Exodus 6:23. He is also identified as the father of Salmon in the book of Ruth 4:20. These relationships place him within a significant family line in the tribe of Judah.
scriptureSignificance: Nahshon's importance in Scripture stems from his leadership of the tribe of Judah during the Exodus, a critical period in Israel's history. As head of his tribe during the census, he played a key role in organizing the people for their journey and service. His lineage also connects him to the broader biblical narrative through his son Salmon, linking him to the Messianic line.
